hints.title: Add the original inequalities
hints.recap: Adding same-direction inequalities gives a valid global consequence.
hints.pitfall: Do not multiply inequalities before checking signs.

recall.reminder: Operations on inequalities must respect the signs of the quantities involved.

hints.title: Test a horizontal slice
hints.body: Set y=0 and find the x-values satisfying both premises.
hints.recap: A counterexample must lie inside the region.
hints.pitfall: Checking only one premise is insufficient.
hints.pause: Choose an allowed point on this slice and test the y claim.

recall.reminder: A counterexample must lie inside the region.

hints.title: Explore a negative factor
hints.body: Put u=x+y, v=x−y, so u>6, v>−4. Keep a permitted negative v fixed and increase u.
hints.recap: The factor signs control multiplication of inequalities.
hints.pitfall: Multiplying lower bounds need not bound a product from below.
hints.pause: Use this behaviour to prove or refute the product claim, then combine the three classifications.

recall.reminder: The factor signs control multiplication of inequalities.

solution:
Adding the original inequalities gives 2x>2, hence x>1. Statement 1 always holds.

At(x, y)=(7, 0), both premises hold, but y>5 does not, so statement 2 is not universal.

At(x, y)=(5, 8), x+y=13>6 and x−y=−3>−4. Their product is−39, which is less than−24, disproving statement 3. Multiplying lower bounds did not preserve the required direction because one factor can be negative.

1 only: B.
knowledgePattern: Prove one universal inequality and refute two with feasible points
